sections.label: Refundable Investment Credit introduction
sections.summary: The Refundable Investment Credit, announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at Budget 2024, will be introduced to enhance investment promotion tools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, we will introduce the Refundable Investment Credit (RIC), which was announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at Budget 2024 to enhance our tools for investment promotion.

sections.label: RIC tax credits for companies
sections.summary: Companies awarded the RIC receive tax credits supporting local expenditure in areas like capital investments, R&D, manpower, and freight and logistics for new high-value investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Companies awarded the RIC will receive tax credits to support their local expenditure in areas, such as capital investments, R&D, manpower, and freight and logistics, when they make new investments in high-value and substantive economic activities.

sections.label: R&R scheme expense deduction cap
sections.summary: The R&R scheme allows a deduction for such expenses, capped at S$300,000 every three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The R&R scheme specifically allows a deduction for such expenses, up to a cap of S$300,000 every three years.

sections.label: Expanded qualifying expenditure scope
sections.summary: From Year of Assessment 2025, qualifying expenditure scope expands to include designer and professional fees, now common for renovation works.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, from Year of Assessment (YA) 2025, the scope of qualifying expenditure will be expanded to include designer and professional fees, as it is now common for such fees to be incurred for renovation works.

sections.label: Income Tax Amendment Bill clauses
sections.summary: Clauses 13 and 30 of the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill provide for these amendments, implementing two new top-up taxes from the BEPS 2.0 initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Clauses 13 and 30 of the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill provide for these amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Bill implements two new top-up taxes, arising from the BEPS 2.0 initiative.

sections.label: DTT and MTT application rules
sections.summary: DTT and MTT apply to large MNE groups with annual group revenue of €750 million or more, from financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: DTT and MTT will apply to large multinational enterprise (MNE) groups – those with annual group revenue of €750 million or more in at least two of the four preceding financial years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: DTT and MTT will apply from businesses' financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: DTT will apply to the Singapore entities of a large MNE group and will be payable if the group's effective tax rate in Singapore is below 15%.

sections.label: MTT revenue use and funds
sections.summary: Asks the estimated additional revenue from enforcing the Bill and whether it can fund a dedicated MTT fund, RIC and RIE 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the estimated additional revenue from enforcing this Bill in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will these funds be directed to improve public infrastructure, healthcare and workforce development?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest the creation of a dedicated fund to ensure that MTT revenues are reinvested into areas that directly benefit Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, could the increased tax revenue be used to support initiatives, such as the RIC or the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 plan?

sections.label: MNE hub attractiveness incentives
sections.summary: Asks how the Bill keeps Singapore an attractive MNE hub and suggests tax incentives for MNE workforce reinvestment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Bill ensure that Singapore remains an attractive hub for MNEs, even while adhering to global tax regulations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest introducing additional tax incentives for MNEs to reinvest their savings into local workforce development, which will benefit both businesses and our workers.

sections.label: Engagement and global tax fairness
sections.summary: Urges engagement with MNEs, SMEs and public, notes Singapore's convention commitments and the 15% corporate minimum tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to engage closely with MNEs, SMEs and the public to implement this Bill, ensuring it leads to sustainable growth, innovation and shared prosperity for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is our opportunity to ensure that Singapore continues to lead on the global stage while protecting the interests of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us take decisive action to make sure that this Bill not only promotes global tax fairness, but also builds a more resilient and equitable future for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that Singapore has been a signatory of the original convention since mid-2017 and, four years thence, having signed on to the second phase, this is essentially a ratification of our pre-existing international commitments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, the stipulations give effect to a corporate minimum tax that, absent action on our part, as Minister Indranee has shared, would simply afford other jurisdictions the opportunity to apply a top-up tax, if our effective rates were to fall below the minimum threshold of 15%.

sections.label: ASEAN corporate tax comparison
sections.summary: States that a 15% corporate tax rate remains below the ASEAN regional average of a little more than 20%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, even compared to our ASEAN neighbors, a corporate tax rate at the 15% minimum remains below the regional average of a little more than 20%.

sections.label: Singapore competitiveness ranking factors
sections.summary: Cites the World Competitiveness Report ranking Singapore top three for labour market, trade openness and infrastructure, and 10th for tax policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the World Competitiveness Report, Singapore owes its competitiveness landscape more to our efficient labour market, openness to international trade and investment, and educational and technological infrastructure, all of which we rank in the top three globally, other than our tax policy, where we place 10th.

sections.label: Reinvesting BEPS 2.0 excess revenue
sections.summary: States the Government plans to reinvest any excess revenue from BEPS 2.0 participation back into the economy for competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government has, for its part, made it clear that it plans to reinvest any excess revenue garnered from participation in BEPS 2.0 back into the economy to ensure competitiveness.

sections.label: Refundable Investment Credits caution
sections.summary: Speaker cautions against Refundable Investment Credits becoming a loophole and urges channelling BEPS 2.0 top-up tax proceeds into intangible capital and worker skills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even in the most recent context of Prime Minister Wong's Budget Statement this year, I cautioned against the Refundable Investment Credits scheme morphing into some kind of loophole for simply increasing production, rather than R&D or green transition efforts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I will reiterate the appeal here: that as we reinvest the proceeds from the top-up taxes accruing from BEPS 2.0, we once again consciously channel these toward bolstering our intangible capital, the education and skills of our workers, to generate knowledge and ideas that would keep us at the forefront of the global competitiveness frontier.

sections.label: Carbon pricing and CBAM
sections.summary: Despite slow global carbon pricing progress, the EU's go-it-first CBAM has sparked complementary legislation in other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As frustrating as the lack of progress in carbon pricing worldwide has been, especially for those of us that are advocates of the approach, the go-it-first strategy of the EU in implementing its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), it is heartening to see how unilateral approaches have nevertheless sparked complementary legislation in other jurisdictions.

sections.label: Refreshing growth model
sections.summary: Speaker says Singapore must embrace BEPS 2.0 and channel energies toward people and their embedded knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this reason, we should, nay, we must, not only embrace the spirit of BEPS 2.0 for our economy, but proactively channel our energies to refreshing our growth model toward the genuine drivers in the 21st century: our people and the knowledge embedded in them.

sections.label: Global minimum corporate tax
sections.summary: The changes align with international tax standards and introduce a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate for large MNEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These changes represent an important step in our ongoing efforts to align with international tax standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They introduce a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for large MNEs.

sections.label: Affected MNEs and relocations
sections.summary: About 1,800 MNEs in Singapore with revenues above €750 million have effective tax rates below 15% and will be affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Around 1,800 MNEs in Singapore with global revenues above €750 million have an effective tax rate below 15% and thee are the entities that will be affected by the new rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the financial impact of the Pillar Two rules will only play out in FY2027, has the Government, at this stage, identified any specific industries or sectors within the country that are likely to be negatively impacted by the global minimum tax?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Have any MNEs already indicated that they will relocate as a result of the MMT Bill and if so, what steps has the Government taken or will it be taking to manage any detrimental effects of these relocations?

sections.label: Surcharges and penalties
sections.summary: Clause 46 imposes surcharges for failure to register and Part 8 lists offences and penalties under the new law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As set out in clause 46 of the Bill, surcharges are imposed where MNE groups fail to register and Part 8 of the Bill lists a string of offences and penalties that entities could be exposed to under the new law.

sections.label: Arts survey quality of life
sections.summary: The National Arts Council's 2023 Population Survey on the Arts found 75% of respondents agreed arts and culture improved quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to National Arts Council's 2023 Population Survey on the Arts, 75% of respondents agreed that arts and culture had the effect of improving one's quality of life.

sections.label: Creative arts and foreign investment
sections.summary: Studies link creative occupations to high-tech industry growth, and EDB cites Singapore's creative arts scene to investors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: His studies have shown that a high number of creative occupations can be a strong predictor of a region's high-tech industry concentration, density and employment growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In its assurance to potential foreign investors and expatriates that Singapore offers an excellent quality of life for its citizens and residents, the Economic Development Board (EDB) itself refers to the country's "lively creative arts scene." As we move forward in a BEPS 2.0 tax environment for foreign investment, I hope the Government continues to prioritise the funding and development of our arts and cultural groups.

sections.label: Minimum effective tax rate MNEs
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a 15% minimum effective tax rate for large MNEs with at least €750 million annual consolidated group revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One of the key provisions of the Bill is the introduction of a minimum effective tax rate of 15% for large MNEs that have a consolidated group revenue of at least €750 million annually in at least two of the four preceding financial years.

sections.label: Corporate tax revenue increase
sections.summary: IRAS announced corporate tax revenues rose by $5.9 billion in FY2023 to $29 billion, 36% of total tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: IRAS announced last month that corporate tax revenues increased by $5.9 billion in FY2023, reaching $29 billion or 36% of total tax revenues.

sections.label: MNE tax dependence and SMEs
sections.summary: The OECD found Singapore fourth-most dependent on large MNEs for corporate tax revenue; the speaker suggests investing some revenue in SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The OECD's Corporate Tax Statistics report found that we are the fourth-most dependent economy on large MNEs for corporate tax revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Instead of pouring all the additional tax revenue back into more economic support for MNEs, we can invest part of the additional revenue in our SMEs, which employed 71% of our workforce as of 2023, and help them leverage on AI and other new technologies, so that they can become more productive and internationally competitive, and hopefully grow into local MNEs of our own.

sections.label: Tax rates by company profit
sections.summary: Companies with pre-tax profits of $200,000 to $10 million pay 8% to 9% in taxes, while those exceeding $1 billion pay under 1%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Companies with pre-tax profits between $200,000 and $10 million pay an average of 8% to 9% of their profits as taxes, while companies with profits exceeding $1 billion pay less than 1%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The minimum effective tax rate introduced by this Bill will top up the effective tax rate of the high-profit multinational enterprises in Singapore to 15%.

sections.label: PSP proposal for tax revenue
sections.summary: PSP proposes investing additional tax revenue in SMEs for AI, productivity, competitiveness, and in measures to cut business and living costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP believes that we should invest the additional tax revenue brought by this Bill into our SMEs, helping them utilise artificial intelligence and other new technologies to improve productivity and international competitiveness, potentially helping them to become multinational companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The additional tax revenue can also provide resources for the Government to take measures to help businesses reduce operating costs, help Singaporeans reduce living costs, and continue to attract foreign investment at a lower cost.

sections.label: GloBE rules revenue threshold
sections.summary: The GloBE rules apply to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least €750 million annually in two of four preceding years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Broadly speaking, the GloBE rules apply to a multinational enterprises (MNE) group that has a consolidated group revenue of at least €750 million annually in at least two of the four preceding financial years.

sections.label: US firms' Singapore effective tax rate
sections.summary: An article states 65% of US firms' foreign profits are in low-tax jurisdictions, with US companies' effective Singapore tax rate at 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the article, "65% of US firms foreign profits are in low-tax jurisdictions, such as Ireland and Singapore, tax-havens like Bermuda, or in stateless entities." What I find most interesting is the finding that the effective tax rate for US companies in Singapore based on the filings is a mere 4% instead of our statutory tax rate of 17%.

sections.label: Lawrence Wong on revenue estimates
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong suggested Singapore's revenue range could be $2 billion to $11 billion yearly, with detailed estimates to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Subsequently in his round up speech, then-Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong suggested that based on data points from the OECD, Hong Kong and Switzerland, the range for Singapore could be anywhere from around $2 billion to $11 billion a year and that the Government will provide its own detailed revenue estimates in due course.

sections.label: Refunds and RIC information availability
sections.summary: Unutilised credits are refunded in cash within four years, but substantive RIC information was not seen despite promised availability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Any unutilised credits will be refunded to the company in cash within four years when the company satisfies the conditions for receiving the credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The list of economic activities and qualifying expenditure categories specified by IRAS, however, appear to be notably broad-based in scope and wider than the tax credit schemes in some other jurisdictions, which primarily focus on R&D activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While more information was said to be available on the EDB and EnterpriseSG websites by 3Q 2024, it is now mid-October and, to date, I have not been able to see any substantive information on RICs thus far.

sections.label: RIC cash payout option
sections.summary: Sections 30 to 32 let a company choose to receive RIC in cash instead of offsetting Corporate Income Tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, even though each RIC award will have a qualifying period of up to 10 years and that the credits are supposed to be offset against Corporate Income Tax payable, subsections 30 to 32 effectively enables the company to choose to receive the RIC in cash ahead of the payout date specified, in lieu of being used to offset taxes.

sections.label: Government position on STTR
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for the Government's position on STTR, noting the MNE Bill is silent on it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As such, may I ask the Minister what is the Government's position on STTR, given that this MNE Bill is, as far as I observe, silent on STTR?

sections.label: Adhering to BEPS 2.0 principles
sections.summary: The passage argues that not adhering to BEPS 2.0 returns to a race to the bottom, and that MNEs should pay their fair share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Should we decide not to adhere to the principles of BEPS 2.0, we once again return to the vicious race to the bottom where countries compete to offer the lowest tax rates in a bid to attract corporate profits, undermining fair competition, penalising smaller local SMEs that cannot engage in aggressive tax planning and, ultimately, weakens national and international economies by depriving it of the resources necessary for sustainable development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is only fair that MNEs, which benefit from our skilled workforce, advanced infrastructure and stable regulatory environment, pay their proportionate and fair share of taxes and contribute to our nation building.

sections.label: MTT, DTT and double taxation
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill introduces MTT and DTT for a 15% minimum tax on MNEs and asks how double taxation will be prevented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, this is the function of Government, to direct our operating revenues, such as from income taxes, into operating and development expenditures across a range of areas, such as healthcare, education and defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But it is an entirely different thing to roundtrip additional income received from in-scope corporates, back to the same corporates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope the additional tax revenues from BEPS 2.0 will not simply be in substance returned to MNEs through other forms but invested in Singaporeans and our collective future instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill, through the introduction of MTT and DTT, represents a significant step in ensuring that MNEs pay a minimum tax of 15%, reinforcing Singapore's commitment to international tax transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While we welcome this alignment, I would like to ask the Minister: how will the Government ensure that these new rules, while in line with international standards, will prevent double taxation for Singapore-based entities?

sections.label: DTT exclusions for entities
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill includes joint ventures with 50% or more parent ownership, while certain investment and insurance entities are excluded from the DTT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the Bill includes joint ventures, where the parent holds 50% or more of the ownership interest, certain investment and insurance entities are excluded from the DTT.

sections.label: Tiered penalties and tax revenues
sections.summary: The passage suggests a tiered penalty structure and anticipates that MTT and DTT will increase Singapore's tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government explore a tiered penalty structure to balance enforcement with fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is anticipated that the introduction of the MTT and DTT will increase tax revenues for Singapore.

sections.label: Foreign firms employing residents
sections.summary: The passage cites a Straits Times article and MOM data that 20% of firms are foreign-owned but employ 60% of residents in high-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a recent The Straits Times article and data released by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), while only 20% of firms in Singapore are foreign-owned, they employ 60% of Singapore residents in high-paying jobs.

sections.label: BEPS Pillar Two top-up taxes
sections.summary: Parent entities of MNE groups in Singapore and Singapore subsidiaries of foreign MNEs will be subject to top-up taxes under BEPS Pillar Two rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both parent entities of MNE groups in Singapore and Singapore subsidiaries of foreign MNEs will be directly impacted, as they will be subject to top-up taxes under the BEPS Pillar Two rules.

sections.label: MNE registration deadline and penalty
sections.summary: MNE groups in scope for the financial year ending 31 December 2025 must register by 30 June 2026, or face a 10% penalty of total top-up tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For MNE groups falling within the scope for the financial year ending 31 December 2025, the registration deadline will be 30 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Failure to meet this deadline could result in a penalty of 10% of the total top-up tax, which could amount to a significant sum for large corporations.

sections.label: Refundable Investment Credit for businesses
sections.summary: The Income Tax (Amendment) Bill introduces the Refundable Investment Credit under new section 93B, offering tax credits of up to 50% of qualifying expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Turning to the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill, the Government's introduction of the Refundable Investment Credit (RIC), under a new section 93B of the Income Tax Act, is a timely and strategic measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The RIC offers businesses tax credits of up to 50% of qualifying expenditure, which is particularly valuable for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

sections.label: Expanding RIC to green investments
sections.summary: Under the Singapore Green Plan 2030, the RIC should be expanded to cover green investments such as energy efficiency, carbon reduction and sustainable production.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As part of the Singapore Green Plan 2030, the RIC should be expanded to cover green investments, such as energy efficiency projects, carbon reduction technologies and sustainable production practices.

sections.label: Support for both Bills
sections.summary: The speaker supports both Bills despite the clarification and recommendations made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarification and recommendations, I support both the Bills.

sections.label: Singapore's response to BEPS Pillar Two
sections.summary: The Bill responds to the OECD's BEPS framework, particularly Pillar Two, which addresses tax avoidance and profit shifting by large corporations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By keeping pace with global competition through these tax credits, Singapore enhances its abilities to attract substantial investments, ensuring long-term economic growth and segmenting its position as a premier business destination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill is Singapore's response to the OECD's BEPS framework, particularly Pillar Two, which seeks to address tax avoidance and profit shifting by large corporations.

sections.label: Minimum tax and business challenges
sections.summary: The 15% minimum tax protects Singapore's tax base and reputation, but the Bills could pose challenges for businesses, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 15% minimum tax helps Singapore protect its tax base by closing loopholes that allow profit shifting to lower-tax jurisdictions, ensuring that large corporations contribute to our nation's development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, by complying with the OECD's global tax framework and aligning our income tax policies with international practices, Singapore strengthens its reputation as a transparent, ethical and business-friendly hub, which will continue to attract foreign investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, despite many positive outcomes for the overall economy, these Bills could lead to certain challenges for businesses especially for SMEs.

sections.label: SMEs and RIC eligibility
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SMEs can also benefit from the RIC or whether it is primarily designed for larger corporations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Five, can SMEs also benefit from the RIC or is it primarily designed for larger corporations?

sections.label: Singapore investment and global competition
sections.summary: Singapore ranks 14th in the 2023 Milken Institute Global Opportunity Index, with FDI inflows rising from S$1.73 trillion in 2018 to S$2.62 trillion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singapore remains a top investment destination, ranked 14th globally in the 2023 Milken Institute Global Opportunity Index, with foreign direct investment inflows rising from S$1.73 trillion in 2018 to S$2.62 trillion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Countries are actively attracting investments: Japan announced a $18 billion package to boost its semiconductor industry; the United States (US) catalysed $450 billion in investments under the CHIPS Act; and Malaysia aims to secure US$107 billion in semiconductor investments.

sections.label: RIC as qualified refundable tax credit
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong confirmed in his 2024 Budget Statement that the RIC qualifies as a qualified refundable tax credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong confirmed in his 2024 Budget Statement that the RIC qualifies as a qualified refundable tax credit.

sections.label: RIC budget and funding
sections.summary: The passage asks what the total budget for the RIC is and how it will be funded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is the total budget for RIC and how will it be funded?

sections.label: RIC mischaracterisation and funding caution
sections.summary: The passage cautions against double dipping revenue and mischaracterising the RIC as enabling avoidance of the minimum effective tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And worse, double dipping an unpredictable revenue to cover both healthcare costs and grants for investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I would also like to caution against the mischaracterisation of investment incentives, such as the Refundable Investment Credit (RIC), as enabling avoidance of the minimum effective tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister highlighted in his Budget speech, the RIC qualifies as a qualified refundable tax credit scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is evident that the design of this initiative is not intended to provide a tax haven but rather to function as a grant aimed at attracting the right investments into Singapore.

sections.label: Countries implementing MMT Bill
sections.summary: Some countries have begun moving legislation to implement IRR and TTT, while others have not started implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On my last point on timing of implementing the MMT Bill, while countries like Hong Kong, Ireland, Switzerland, Malaysia, Vietnam and Australia have begun to move legislation to implement IRR and TTT, there are other countries which have not started implementation, such as the US, the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia, China and India.

sections.label: RIC tax credit offset and refund
sections.summary: RIC tax credits offset corporate income tax payable first, and unutilised credits are refunded within four years, consistent with GLoBE rules.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Tax credits under the RIC will be offset against corporate income tax payable in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The refund of unutilised credits within four years from the time the company makes the claim application is consistent with the GLoBE rules for qualified refundable tax credits.

sections.label: NPF top-up at Budget 2024
sections.summary: The NPF was topped up at Budget 2024 with S$2 billion to support the RIC and other investment promotion efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Member might recall that we had topped up the NPF at Budget 2024 with S$2 billion to support the RIC and other investment promotion efforts.

sections.label: DTT tops up effective tax rate
sections.summary: If a large MNE group's effective tax rate on Singapore profits is below 15%, the DTT will top it up to 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: If a large MNE group's effective tax rate on its Singapore profits is below 15%, the DTT will top up its effective tax rate to 15%.

sections.label: Singapore interest in DTT and MTT
sections.summary: Without DTT and MTT, affected MNE groups would pay top-up tax to other jurisdictions, so Singapore should implement both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: If we do not impose the DTT and MTT, affected MNE groups will have to pay the top-up tax to other jurisdictions instead.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, it is in Singapore's interest to push ahead with the implementation of both DTT and MTT so that we do not cede tax revenue to other jurisdictions.

sections.label: IRAS light-touch penalty approach
sections.summary: IRAS will adopt a light-touch approach to penalties in initial years if an MNE group shows reasonable measures for GloBE rules.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To allay businesses’ concerns regarding penalties, IRAS will adopt a light-touch approach in the initial years of implementation, if an MNE group can demonstrate that it has taken reasonable measures to ensure the correct application of the GloBE rules.

sections.label: DTT and MTT revenue timing
sections.summary: DTT or MTT revenue will only be collected from FY2027, as mentioned by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong during the Budget debate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong during the Budget debate this year, any DTT or MTT revenue will only be collected from FY2027.

sections.label: Funding healthcare for ageing population
sections.summary: Structural revenue-raising moves including the GST increase fund healthcare expenditure for an ageing population, with an Assurance Package to cushion the impact.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, with consequent increases in healthcare expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: That is why, rather than waiting for revenues that are uncertain and which would be too late, we have made structural revenue-raising moves, including the GST increase, to fund this expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have planned ahead for this and supported Singaporeans with a substantial Assurance Package to cushion the impact.

sections.label: Singapore's strengths and rankings
sections.summary: Mr Louis Chua cited strengths such as robust infrastructure and a well-established legal system, and rankings including second in the IMD World Talent Ranking.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Chua also highlighted other strengths, such as having robust infrastructure and a well-established legal system, and he cited many proof points, including the fact that Singapore was ranked second in the IMD World Talent Ranking, that we were fourth in the World Financial Centre's ranking and, in June 2024, Singapore took top spot in the IMD World Competitive Rankings.

sections.label: Investing DTT and MTT revenue
sections.summary: Additional DTT and MTT revenue will be used to invest in areas including broadband, artificial intelligence infrastructure, Changi Airport Terminal 5 and Tuas Mega Port.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These are important factors that businesses consider when making an investment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will use the additional revenue from the DTT and MTT to invest significantly in many of these areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our investments into future infrastructure, for example, put us in good stead for sustainable and resilient future growth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These include the upgrading of our nationwide broadband network and artificial intelligence infrastructure, Changi Airport Terminal 5, Tuas Mega Port, as well as critical infrastructure to facilitate Singapore’s transition to cleaner energy and safeguard our energy security.

sections.label: Initiatives for SMEs
sections.summary: Initiatives targeted at SMEs include the double tax deduction for internationalisation, the SMEs Go Digital programme and the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have introduced many initiatives targeted at our SMEs, such as the double tax deduction for internationalisation, the SMEs Go Digital programme and the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Rules Review committee
sections.summary: In April this year, the Government set up an Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review to improve regulatory efficiency and reduce compliance burden for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In April this year, the Government set up an Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review to oversee Government efforts to improve regulatory efficiency and reduce compliance burden for our SMEs and help them to better navigate Government rules and regulations.

sections.label: Tax system investment provisions
sections.summary: The provisions aim to anchor high-quality investments, keep the tax system relevant and fair, and match international tax developments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The provisions seek to anchor high-quality investments in Singapore, ensure that our tax system remains relevant and fair to businesses and individuals, and keep Singapore in step with international tax developments.

sections.label: MNE relocation limiting revenue gains
sections.summary: The speaker said MNEs could relocate operations or headquarters, limiting sustainable gains, a point Minister Indranee Rajah also mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: If he would have heard my speech, I mentioned that while it may increase short-term revenue, MNEs could adjust strategies by relocating operations of headquarters, limiting the sustainable gains – something which Minister Indranee Rajah has also mentioned.

sections.label: RIC annual net fiscal impact
sections.summary: The passage asks what the estimated net fiscal impact of the RIC is on an annual basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Correspondingly, what is the estimated net fiscal impact of the RIC on an annual basis?

sections.label: RIC credits and IRAS guidance
sections.summary: RIC credits go to those investing in high-value substantive activities, and IRAS needs time to work on guidance and timelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Essentially, the ones that can get the RIC credits would be those who make investments in high-value and substantive economic activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: All of these are part of how they can basically add to or grow our economy and support our green transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And on the question of guidance and timelines, give IRAS a little time to work on that.

sections.label: International tax education resources
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government plans to devote more resources to international tax education at tertiary level or beyond.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does the Government have any plans at this point in time to devote more resources to the development of international tax education in Singapore at the tertiary level or beyond?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The short answer is that we would love to, but we are always being called upon to give people education on many things.

sections.label: Tax education in Economics modules
sections.summary: The Government will work with MOE on Economics modules, and points to IRAS and BEPS websites.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Where possible, we will work with MOE to see what can be included in the general Economics modules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Obviously, students in the Institutes of Higher Learning will have to deal with it, if they are dealing with tax modules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But other than that, I would say that the IRAS website is a good place to start and so are the BEPS websites.
